semantics.NOT RUN: the scenario produced no observation record at all
semantics.BLOCKED: the scenario or a precondition recorded that it could not be exercised (absent module, undefined differential); never a pass
semantics.FAIL: an observation contradicts a predicate, or a required observation is missing from a scenario that ran
semantics.PASS: every predicate held on the recorded raw observations; says nothing beyond the named row

reasons.NC7-01..03: Architect ruling Q2 requires three mandatory negative controls that no earlier row stated as such: (1) unauthorized execution must not commit an effect; (2) stale or mismatched authority must prevent an unauthorized effect; (3) missing, invalid or expired required evidence must not permit execution. Expected verdicts are computed from raw observations recorded by suites/mvp-chain/_chain.py scenario nc_authority_gates (status, attempted, error text, independent read-only effect count, claim state), never from a desired outcome; an authorized control case through the same Ctx must commit exactly one effect so a refusal cannot be an artefact of a harness that cannot commit. The predicates require refusal, not attempted, and zero effects; they do not pin error strings (recorded for readers). Existing rows that overlap: NC1-01..05 (revocation), NC3-01..03 (duplicates), NC4-02 (ingress adversarial inputs: effect count unchanged); they are cited as related evidence, not re-used as these rows, because none of them observes a never-issued claim, a not-authorized decision, an expired claim, an advanced revision, an envelope mismatch or any evidence state.

limitations.os_level_process_kill: UNQUALIFIED. True OS-level process kill and crash recovery are not exercised by any row. NC2-01..06, ruling 4 and NC6-02/03 use the existing synthetic fault injection (simulate='lost_ack', an owner-side post-commit wrapper, an unavailable or unreadable store). Accepted for the 2026-10-31 target under architect ruling Q2 unless the MVP claim promises OS-kill recovery; if it does, this stays UNQUALIFIED/INCOMPLETE.
limitations.nc4_03_source_predicate_v5: NC4-03 is a SOURCE-LEVEL, narrowly scoped static predicate (v5, builder-prepared after the independent Q1 review; no taint-analysis subsystem, no ingress change). v5 adds: literal-only protected keywords (attempt_id, budget_id, expires_at, decision_input_commitment, decision_input_profile_version, now except host.now) on execute/provision_claim/decide, and RuntimeProposal update keys (evidence_refs, risk_metadata, run_id, expires_at, not_before, expected_side_effects, tenant_id); no attribute stores, setattr or object.__setattr__ on non-self objects; no model_validate/model_construct/__class__/__dict__; no non-literal positional arguments into ExecutionOperation, ExecutionEnvelope, execute or provision_claim; import-as, match-capture, except-as and def/class rebinding of the tracked names; a separate recursive check of everything under tools/mvp_ingress (exact list of 7 regular files incl. BOUNDARY.md, no directory, symlink or extension module, recursive sha256); ast_digest pins honoured only on CPython 3.13 (ast.dump differs across 3.11/3.12/3.13). The *.py tree digest ea37100d... that the pins bind is unchanged.
limitations.nc4_03_not_covered_not_claimed: NOT FIXABLE HERE and NOT CLAIMED as covered: (1) hub-root or standard-library name shadowing through the current-directory-first sys.path when the ingress runs `python -m tools.mvp_ingress.server` (would need -P or -I, an ingress change, i.e. an architect escalation); (2) IPC peer authentication default allowed_uids=None; (3) Yama/ptrace and other host properties; (4) Control Plane and Runtime code is not followed (imports are not followed); (5) values under non-prohibited fixed keys, and mutation by a helper that receives a non-authority-named object, are not taint-tracked.
limitations.executor_level_scope_of_NC7: NC7-01..03 are executor-level controls on route B at the candidate tuple (Runtime c5e97e87). They are not ingress-level evidence (NC4-01..03 and NC2-06 are), and they say nothing about code with direct access to the destination database or the authority writers (see the D2 REACHABLE characterisations, which are recorded and not mandatory).
limitations.launch_isolation_scope: NC4-04 is code-level launch isolation evidence taken from the live ingress process's argv and the refusal of the old entry point. It does not qualify the host (Yama, dedicated identities; see the environment record) and says nothing about a tampered interpreter, stdlib or site-packages.
limitations.launch_precheck_scope: Hub-recorded limitation: the launcher's pre-checks emulate source, package and extension files only. A stray sourceless .pyc, a zip, an __init__ extension module or a site-packages `tools` package may run before the launcher refuses, or crash it (fail-closed); this is outside NC4-04 and NC4-03 coverage.

result_layers.rule: Four layers are reported separately and are never aggregated into an NC4 PASS: (1) engineering complete/incomplete; (2) individual mandatory controls, with code-level provenance (NC4-03, NC4-04) identified as BUILDER-SIDE until independently adjudicated, and host isolation evidence (NC4-01/NC4-02 observations, environment record G-11) reported separately; (3) overall independent acceptance; (4) release readiness (HOLD).
result_layers.wording: Code-level ingress provenance was demonstrated through independent source review and builder-side testing. Host process isolation was not independently qualified under the original restricted-host profile. NC4 remains INCOMPLETE.
